messages.subject: BioGeoBEARS new stuff
parts:
(oops, meant to send this as a new thread)

Hi all BioGeoBEARS users,

I've refactored some code and moved some functions etc. so there are some new files to source; the full list is below (also in the PhyloWiki script).  Let me know if issues remain after sourcing the full list. 

I have added some new features, I will do an official announcement at some point (hopefully I can get this all on CRAN soon). The ones that might be most interesting to play with: 

1. A new parameter, "w", which is an exponent on the manual dispersal multipliers matrix (so you can test whether your manual dispersal multipliers might be a better explanation if taken to some power, rather than just being forced to fix your manual dispersal multipliers to your best guesses.  w=1 (default) means the manual dispersal multipliers are used unchanged (as normal). w=0 would mean the manual dispersal multipliers are all rescaled to 1, etc.  This doesn't solve all issues with manual dispersal multipliers but may help reduce subjectivity there.

2. A new parameter, "n", which is an exponent on an "environmental distances matrix". This works identically to the regular distances matrix and x exponent; but having the second matrix lets you add a second sort of distance between areas, e.g. environmental distance or whatever you like. I am dubious about how often you will be able to get statistical support for this (with 3-10 areas, there aren't that many different distances on which to fit these parameters), but it can be tried at least.

3. I've added an area adjacency matrix file option, which should work like the one in python Lagrange. It works just like areas_allowed, by removing states that don't match, but the interpretive code is different than areas_allowed, so that it matches the Lagrange likelihoods.  This should work for both normal and stratified analyses. Note that, with this method, you cannot e.g. exclude ABD but keep ABCD in the state space. If you want to do such a thing (can you justify allowing ABCD but disallowing ABD?), you could do it by manually modifying the states_list (or lists_of_states_lists_0based for stratified runs) and storing these in the BioGeoBEARS run object. As usual, you have to ensure that your state space allows the included states to be connected so that your data has a likelihood greater than 0 (ln likelihood greater than -Inf).

4. The stratum boundaries are now plotted on time-stratified output plots by default.

Let me know if issues arise. Cheers!
Nick
